customfield_10020.name: Sprint 9
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal
1. [MM F3] Control Tower — deliver the route-level view end to end: expandable trip rows with
all stops, route Quick View and the new Trip Detail (header, map, per-delivery tabs and full
journey with evidence), so Middle Mile dispatchers follow a whole route instead of a single
delivery.
2. [CT-Filters] Close the filters package (date, active alert, clear filters) and guarantee that
real-time updates respect the active filters, so the board a dispatcher filtered stays the board
they are looking at.
3. Once we confirm the discoveries for Lanes and Operation Type with the other tech teams, we
will move forward with the cards that have no interdependencies.
4. Time to address the bugs left in the backlog (Tech Support and Slots items were included in
the current sprint).
5. Continue the platform clean-up: finish the CDN migration validation with INF and close the
React 18 upgrade.

Main deliveries
- Control Tower route view: expandable trip rows, route Quick View and Trip Detail (header, map,
per-delivery tabs, full journey + evidence carousel).
- Control Tower filters: date, active alert and clear filters, with real-time respecting them.
- Header decision data: Average Cost/KM card and current ETA with SLA delta.
- Companies: high-privilege endpoint for company name change and Context Menu Pt2.
- Backlog clean-up: Tech Support fixes (report column, Log in as Company, company hierarchy) and
the Slots notification defect.
- CDN migration validation with INF and React 18 upgrade closure.

Sprint Constraints
- Half of the sprint is carryover: 12 items / 52.5 SP came from Sprint 8, several already in Code
Review or Pending QA on day 1.
- No public holiday in Brazil within the sprint window (Sept 8th–22nd).
- [days off / vacations to confirm]

Risks
- The Lanes and Operation Type models are still in discovery; cards depending on them may not
start in this sprint.
- The end-to-end homologation of the 15 Amazon alerts depends on the alert payload being
available from INF.
- The CDN migration validation depends on INF reviewing the comments on the merged PRs.

Validations
- Validation with the other tech teams regarding the Lanes and Operation Type models.
- Validation with INF on the CDN migration PRs.
- End-to-end homologation of the 15 Amazon alerts.

customfield_10020.name: Sprint 8
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal:

Close out Phase 3 of Control Tower by shipping the full filtering suite (Operation Type, Shipper/Client, Active Alert, Date, Lanes), the multi-stop trip navigation (Table, QuickView, and Trip Detail), and trip-list pagination — consolidating the Middle Mile monitoring foundation ahead of the final polish phase before the September delivery.

The 5 fronts that spanned all of Phase 3:

Alerts & Act Now (real-time prioritization and action queue) — from the initial Exception Control Tower concept through real-time alert delivery and UI severity coding.
KPI Header — the executive metrics bar, from initial UI/endpoint work through SLA Day and Cost/KM cards.
Multi-Stop Journey & Trip Detail — the evolution from single-delivery views to a full-route experience across the trips table, quick view, and trip detail page.
Global & Advanced Filters — from the original filtering discovery to the complete filter suite (Operation Type, Shipper, Active Alert, Date, Lanes, Saved Filters).
Data Foundation — the backend layer (lane persistence, ETA/SLA, alert case schema, pagination) underpinning the other four fronts.

customfield_10020.name: Sprint 8
customfield_10020.goal:
Sprint Goal:

Close out Phase 3 of Control Tower by shipping the full filtering suite (Operation Type, Shipper/Client, Active Alert, Date, Lanes), the multi-stop trip navigation (Table, QuickView, and Trip Detail), and trip-list pagination — consolidating the Middle Mile monitoring foundation ahead of the final polish phase before the September delivery.

Global & Advanced Filters — from the original filtering discovery to the complete filter suite (Operation Type, Shipper, Active Alert, Date, Lanes, Saved Filters).
Data Foundation — the backend layer (lane persistence, ETA/SLA, alert case schema, pagination) underpinning the other four fronts.
